review_candidates.title: Consultant - Diaspora Engagement, Partnerships and Investment
review_candidates.description: Job Description The Streamlining Diaspora Engagement to Catalyze Private Investments and Entrepreneurship for Enhanced Resilience (SDE4R) project aims to strengthen private sector development and socio-economic resilience through diaspora engagement, including diaspora investment, skills transfer, financial inclusion initiatives, humanitarian and resilience support, and diaspora engagement policy frameworks. The project seeks to create an enabling environment for diaspora participation while leveraging diaspora financial and human capital to support vulnerable populations, micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), women, youth and local communities. The consultancy will provide technical support to advance diaspora engagement, strengthen partnerships with government, private sector, financial institutions and development partners, and support investment and entrepreneurship initiatives. It will also contribute to stakeholder consultations, analysis, knowledge products and reporting to support effective implementation of SDE4R activities. Responsibilities Task 1. Diaspora and Stakeholder Engagement Support the planning and implementation of diaspora engagement activities under SDE4R. Support engagement and consultations with diaspora organizations, government institutions, private-sector actors, financial institutions, development partners and other relevant stakeholders. Assist with the organization and facilitation of meetings, workshops and consultations, including documenting key outcomes and follow-up actions. Task 2. Diaspora Investment, Entrepreneurship and Partnerships Support activities promoting diaspora investment, entrepreneurship, financial inclusion and skills transfer. Assist in identifying and documenting investment, entrepreneurship and partnership opportunities involving diaspora, MSMEs and other private-sector stakeholders. Support stakeholder mapping, partnership engagement and preparation of relevant briefing and technical materials. Task 3. Monitoring, Reporting and Knowledge Management Collect, compile and maintain project and stakeholder information to support monitoring and reporting. Document project results, stakeholder feedback, lessons learned, good practices and success stories. Contribute to reports, briefs, presentations, factsheets, communication materials and other relevant project products. Task 4. Project Implementation and Coordination Support Coordinate with relevant IOM teams and stakeholders to support timely implementation and follow-up of assigned SDE4R activities. Track agreed activities, outputs and follow-up actions and flag implementation issues as appropriate. Perform other related tasks within the scope of the consultancy as assigned. Performance Will Be Assessed Against Quality and relevance of technical advice and inputs provided on diaspora engagement, partnerships, investment and entrepreneurship. Quality and effectiveness of stakeholder engagement and facilitation, including engagement with diaspora, government, private-sector and development stakeholders. Quality, accuracy and usefulness of technical documentation, analysis and knowledge products. Effective contribution to partnership development and investment-related project activities. Timely and professional completion of agreed consultancy tasks and outputs. Effective coordination and communication with IOM and relevant stakeholders. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education: Bachelors in migration and development, diaspora engagement, private-sector development, entrepreneurship, investment facilitation, financial inclusion, programme/project management, or a related field. Skills: Strong analytical, organizational, coordination, written communication, report-writing, facilitation and stakeholder-engagement skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, monitor activities and data, and prepare high-quality technical documents, presentations, briefs and knowledge products. Experience: 3 years relevant experience in programme/project implementation, including donor-funded initiatives; engagement with government, development partners, private sector and civil society; organization of consultations, workshops and technical meetings; data collection, monitoring and reporting. Experience in migration and diaspora programming, communication and visibility is an asset.

review_candidates.title: Case Manager
review_candidates.description: Description Position Summary: The OHM Case Manager provides outreach-driven case management services through the Outreach and Health Ministry (OHM) program. Unlike traditional office-based case management roles, this position actively engages individuals in the community (on the street, at encampments, on outreach vans, and at partner sites) and continues working with them beyond initial contact to complete housing applications, benefits enrollment, and other intensive case management services. This role also develops and maintains quality referral relationships with social service agencies. General Purpose: This role supports individuals experiencing homelessness or housing instability, many of whom are medically vulnerable, in achieving housing stability and improved health outcomes. Position Responsibilities Conduct proactive street outreach through the Health Outreach Bus program, but also through the Street Medicine program, CTA program, Harold Washington Library outreach, and other community-based locations. Shifts may include evenings, weekends, and varied daytime hours. Engage individuals where they are located, build rapport using trauma-informed and harm reduction approaches, and serve as a consistent point of contact. Transition individuals from initial outreach engagement into ongoing, intensive housing case management. Complete housing assessments, applications, and documentation necessary for housing placement and stabilization. Assist clients in obtaining identification, income, benefits, and other documentation required for housing eligibility. Provide follow-up support and navigation through housing placement and stabilization processes. Conduct and/or support Coordinated Entry System (CES) assessments. Serve as (or work toward becoming) a Skilled Assessor within the Coordinated Entry System. Maintain strong working knowledge of Chicago Housing Authority (CHA) processes, eligibility requirements, and housing programs. Collaborate with housing providers, shelters, healthcare providers, and other community partners to support housing placements. Complete accurate and timely data entry in HMIS (Homeless Management Information System) and other required systems (e.g., EHR, ETO). Maintain compliant, audit-ready case files in accordance with government, funder, and agency standards. Develop and maintain referral relationships with social service agencies and housing providers. Resources should cover key needs presented by OHM participants, including but not limited to emergency and transitional housing, health, mental health, and addiction services. Participate in community meetings, needs assessments, case conferencing, and interagency collaborations. Drive outreach vans as scheduled. Support volunteer engagement and represent the program at community events as assigned. Participate in periodic community needs assessments and stay informed about trends impacting people experiencing homelessness in Chicago. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications Must meet all governmental, agency, and/or grantors’ qualifications for the position. Must exhibit the ability and willingness to work individually, as well as part of a team. Detail-oriented self-starter with demonstrated interpersonal skills and a clear sense of professional boundaries.
